relationships.description: The stated benefit is bounded or conditioned by a restriction on the solution space, such as a budget ceiling or mandated technology, that determines how far the value can be pursued.
relationships.evidence: A decision record or value analysis document cites the constraint as limiting, or shaping, the way the stated stakeholder benefit can be delivered.

relationships.description: The stated benefit answers or relates to the external or internal force, such as market pressure or rising cost, that makes that benefit worth pursuing.
relationships.evidence: A business case, strategy document or architecture decision record names the driver as the reason the stakeholder benefit matters.

relationships.description: The stakeholder benefit expresses the worth that reaching the intended end state would bring, which links the value to the goal it motivates or justifies.
relationships.evidence: A goal model, strategy document or value map explicitly ties the stated benefit to the goal it justifies.

relationships.description: The measurable end result is the checkable state through which the stakeholder benefit is realized or evidenced, such as an order-time target backing a 'saves customers time' value.
relationships.evidence: An OKR sheet, benefits-realization plan or KPI dashboard definition maps the outcome's target metric to the stated stakeholder benefit.

relationships.description: The stakeholder is the party for whom the benefit holds worth, and from whose perspective the value is expressed.
relationships.evidence: A stakeholder map, persona document or value proposition canvas names the stakeholder as the recipient of the stated benefit.

relationships.description: One stated benefit is related to another, for example as a component, complement or trade-off of it, within the same value model.
relationships.evidence: A value map or business case groups, decomposes or contrasts the two benefits explicitly, for example listing one as contributing to the other.

notes: Value-to-stakeholder is the only link ArchiMate expects here; the rest use generic associated-with, which hides meaning. Value-to-outcome would read better as outcome 'delivers' value. Value-to-goal would read better as 'supports'. Value-to-constraint is weak: constraints restrict the solution, not value. A self-association on value adds little unless it is meant as an aggregation.
